summit-park-blue-ash: The restroom page says the Canopy restrooms stay open year-round. It does not describe door controls, toilet transfers or adult-changing equipment.
Canopy restrooms will remain open year-round
Outdoor water fountains are turned off for winter and reopen in spring, according to the park’s restroom notice. Bring drinking water during the winter shutdown.
All outdoor water fountains throughout the City will also be turned off for the winter and reopen in the spring.
The main playground is southwest of the Canopy. Its published features include seating with sightlines for parents, passive and active play areas and nearby restrooms.
Located southwest of the Canopy, this award-winning, colorful, one-acre playground features traversable ropes, play mounds, and extra-wide slides.
Other features include an activity wall, ample seating with visibility for parents, passive and active play areas, and restrooms conveniently located just a few steps away.
General park hours are dawn to midnight, but natural spaces, trails, ponds and other unlit areas close at 11 p.m.
Hours Dawn to Midnight Natural spaces, trails, ponds, and other unlit areas of the park close at 11:00 p.m.
The October 21, 2026 alert reports the Water Corridor closed for maintenance. It gives no reopening date.
Water Corridor Temporary Closure The Water Corridor is temporarily closed for maintenance.

For the 2026–27 rink season, sensory-sensitive sessions are listed for December 13 and December 21, 2026, from 11 a.m. to noon. Places are limited and reservations are required. The park describes a calmer, less crowded skate and a quiet sensory item to choose at check-in.

Sensory Sensitive Hours (Limited Spots, Reservation Required) Sunday, December 13 | 11 AM to 12 PM Monday, December 21 | 11 AM to 12 PM Enjoy a calmer, less crowded skate designed for guests who prefer or benefit from a quieter experience. Each skater can choose a quiet sensory item at check in. Space is limited, so reserve your spot today:
The 2026–27 rink page offers free skate helpers on a first-come, first-served basis. It does not describe wheelchair use on the ice, assisted transfers or staff-provided physical support.
Free skate helpers, sponsored by MadTree Parks and Rec , are available on a first-come, first-served basis to help new or young skaters find their balance and confidence on the ice.

The rink’s advertised season is November 14, 2026–January 10, 2027. Regular tickets are sold at the rink, with no online or advance sales; weather can temporarily close it, with updates on the park homepage.
Tickets are available for purchase at the rink only (no online or advance sales).
Weather and temperature changes may temporarily close the rink. A pop-up alert will appear on the Summit Park homepage in the event of a closure.
woodward-theater: The theater opens for scheduled events rather than maintaining general visitor hours. Check the individual show listing; admission for guests under 18 depends on the event.
The Woodward Theater is open when we have events: concerts, films, theater, fundraisers, ticketed events, and anything else open to the public.
I'm under 18. Can I go to a concert at the Woodward? A: It depends on the particular show.

Ziegler Park’s own parking page describes a 400-space, two-level garage, with elevators in the northwest and southwest corners. This describes the nearby garage, not a verified continuous route to the theater.
Ziegler Park's 400-space, two-level, underground parking garage is located directly below the great lawn.
The garage's wide, open parking decks are well-lit and have have three broad stairwells, in addition to elevators that are located at the northwest and southwest corners.

The Ziegler garage’s vehicle entrance and exit are on Sycamore Street, at the published address 1322 Sycamore Street. Automated pay stations allow payment before returning to the vehicle; the operator says the garage is staffed around the clock.
The vehicular entrance/exit is located on Sycamore Street. Automated pay stations allow you to pay for parking before returning to your vehicle.
The garage, which is available to monthly and daily parkers, is open and staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
lindner-family-tennis-center-cincinnati-: The tournament’s interactive map describes limited wheelchair parking directly outside the North Entrance. This does not establish shuttle boarding arrangements or guarantee an available space.
Limited wheelchair parking is available directly outside the North Entrance.
Rideshare pickup and drop-off are at the East Entrance. This is separate from the patron drop-off described by the North Entrance.
Rideshare drop-off and pick-up is located at the East Entrance.
To drop someone off at the entry gates, drive to the patron drop-off located by the North Entrance.
During the tournament, the First Aid center is at the south end of Stadium 3 and north end of the Commons.
If you are in need of first aid, head to the First Aid center located on the south end of Stadium 3 and north end of the Commons.
The map directs visitors needing nursing or rehydration help to the Mercy Health First Aid Center. It does not describe a separate nursing room or its facilities.

Visit the Mercy Health First Aid Center for all your on-site health needs. Whether you need a band aid or more serious medical attention, you're nursing or need to rehydrate, the team from Mercy Health is here to help.
The interactive map identifies misting stations and drinking-water stations for tournament visitors. These descriptions do not establish an indoor cooling room.
Stay cool with one of our misting stations.
Stay hydrated with one of our water stations.

Metal detectors are posted at all entrances. The FAQ says guests are asked to empty their pockets and pass through the detector; it does not explain an alternative screening procedure for medical devices or mobility aids.
Metal detectors will be stationed at all entrances around the grounds. All guests will be asked to empty their pockets and pass through the detector.

Prohibited items found during bag inspection must be returned to the owner’s vehicle or discarded. The tournament says it provides no storage area for them; bags left at a gate remain the owner’s risk.

Prohibited items that are discovered during inspections must either be returned to their owner’s vehicle or discarded. The Lindner Family Tennis Center will not provide a storage area for these items. Any bag left at a gate is left at the owner’s risk.

The detailed water-bottle allowance is one unopened see-through plastic bottle up to 1 liter, or one empty non-see-through water container up to 1 liter. Labels for brands other than the tournament sponsor must be removed before entry.
One unopened see-through plastic bottle of water up to 33.5 ounces/1 liter. If not see-through, one empty water container up to 33.5 ounces/1 liter.
Due to sponsorship exclusivity, if your water bottle has a label other than the tournament sponsor brand, the label must be removed before entering tournament grounds.

The prohibited-items list exempts motorized vehicles associated with a medical need and exempts service animals from its animal restriction. It does not specify device dimensions or assistance with transfers.
Hoverboards, Skateboards, Segways or any motorized vehicle not associated with a medical need

Single-compartment bags such as totes or cinch bags must be at most 12 × 18 × 15 inches and fit on the visitor’s lap or under their seat. Single-strap diaper bags are allowed with a child. Multi-compartment backpacks with multiple shoulder straps are prohibited, and all bags are searched.
Guests will not be permitted to bring backpacks (multi-compartment bag with multiple shoulder straps) into Lindner Family Tennis Center
All bags are subject to a complete and thorough search.
Tote bags, cinch bags and other single compartment bags 12″ x 18″ x 15″ or smaller (bag must fit on lap or under the seat occupied). Single strap diaper bags if accompanied by a child.
